mechanics.name: Diversion
mechanics.currentEffect: After spending 30/25/20 seconds in the Killer's Terror Radius while not in chase, Diversion activates. While crouched and motionless, use the Active Ability button to throw a pebble up to 20 metres, creating a Loud Noise notification and fake Scratch Marks at the landing point. It deactivates after use.
activation: Spend tier time in the Terror Radius while not in chase.
Crouch, remain motionless and use Active Ability.
Ends/deactivates when: Deactivates after the pebble is thrown.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (8.2.0): Reduced the Terror Radius charge time to 30/25/20 seconds.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: Staying near the Killer without being chased charges a pebble that creates a decoy noise and trail.
mechanics.tokenOrStackBehavior: Charges one use after 30/25/20 seconds in Terror Radius outside chase; one pebble per activation.
specialInteractions: Creates a Loud Noise notification and fake Scratch Marks at the pebble landing point.

editorial.summary: Charge near the Killer outside chase, then throw a pebble that creates a fake Loud Noise notification and Scratch Marks 20 metres away.
useCases: Send the Killer toward a plausible false location after a hook or patrol event.
Create fake Scratch Marks at the decoy point.
Use coordinated timing to pull a mobile Killer away from a real objective.
counters: The Killer can recognize implausible notifications or simply ignore them.
Stealth Killers make charging harder because Terror Radius uptime is lower.
A bad throw can point the Killer toward real teammates instead.
pros: Can create both noise and fake trail information.
Shorter modern charge time than historical versions.
cons: Requires Terror Radius charging outside chase.
Easy to use in a way that accomplishes nothing.
analysis: Diversion is one of the game’s better comedy perks because the effect can also be strategically real. A well-timed fake notification can pull a Killer toward a location they believe contains a Survivor or objective mistake.
The fake Scratch Marks help sell the story if the Killer reaches the landing point, but the perk never controls whether the Killer takes the bait in the first place.
Charging requires time in the Terror Radius without being chased, which is easier against territorial standard Killers than stealth or highly mobile ones.
Diversion belongs low because misdirection is probabilistic value. Creative players can manufacture strong moments, but a perk that needs the opponent to believe the lie cannot be consistent.
editorial.verdict: A pebble with a résumé. Diversion can genuinely redirect a Killer, but its power begins and ends with whether the Killer believes you.
